pucap1.q: An outpatient with community-acquired pneumonia has risk factors for resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae and a beta-lactam allergy. Which drug fits?
opts: Cefpodoxime is a cephalosporin, a beta-lactam, so the allergy rules it out; a respiratory fluoroquinolone is the choice.
ruled out by a stated finding
Amoxicillin is a beta-lactam and is ruled out by the allergy; with resistance risk factors and an allergy, a respiratory fluoroquinolone fits.
ruled out by a stated finding
A macrolide alone is first line only when there is no resistance risk; with risk factors and a beta-lactam allergy, a respiratory fluoroquinolone fits.
ruled out by a stated finding
Correct. A respiratory fluoroquinolone (levofloxacin or moxifloxacin) is the alternative to beta-lactam plus macrolide and is good for patients with a beta-lactam allergy.

pucap1.q: Which exposure is a listed risk factor for penicillin-resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae?
opts: Nursing home residence is a criterion for health-care associated pneumonia; the listed exposure for resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae is a child in day care.
Hemodialysis is a criterion for health-care associated pneumonia; the exposure listed for penicillin-resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae is a child in day care.
Crowded adult housing is not on the list; the exposure listed for penicillin-resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae is a child in a day care center.
A child who attends day care
Correct. Exposure to a child in a day care center is listed with age over 65, a beta-lactam within 3 months, alcoholism, immunosuppression and medical comorbidities.

pucap1.q: A patient with acute bronchitis has documented Mycoplasma infection. Which antibiotic is preferred?
opts: Azithromycin is a macrolide, and macrolide resistance is the reason doxycycline is preferred for documented Mycoplasma.
ruled out by a stated finding
Erythromycin is a macrolide; because of macrolide resistance, doxycycline is preferred when Mycoplasma is documented.
ruled out by a stated finding
Correct. Doxycycline is preferred when Mycoplasma is documented, because of macrolide resistance.
A respiratory fluoroquinolone is avoided in acute bronchitis unless there was recent antibiotic exposure; doxycycline is preferred for Mycoplasma.
ruled out by a stated finding

pucap1.io: Identify indications for drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
pucap1.q: An outpatient with community-acquired pneumonia has no risk factors for resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae. Which drug is first line?
opts: Doxycycline is the second-line choice for an outpatient without risk factors; the first-line drug is a macrolide such as azithromycin.
Correct. With no risk of resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae, first line is a macrolide (azithromycin or clarithromycin); doxycycline and minocycline are second line.
A respiratory fluoroquinolone is an option when risk factors for resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae are present; without them a macrolide is first line.
Cefpodoxime is the beta-lactam half of the beta-lactam-plus-macrolide regimen used when resistance risk factors are present; first line here is a macrolide.

pucap1.io: Identify indications for drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
pucap1.q: Which group of pathogens is the common cause of acute bronchitis?
opts: Mycoplasma pneumoniae, Chlamydia pneumoniae and Bordetella pertussis cause acute bronchitis only occasionally; the common causes are respiratory viruses.
Streptococcus and Staphylococcus species are occasional bacterial causes, sometimes secondary to a viral illness; most acute bronchitis is viral.
Correct. The common causes are viruses (rhinovirus, coronavirus, influenza, adenovirus); bacteria are only occasional causes, sometimes secondary to a viral illness.
Gram-negative bacilli are named among the intensive care unit pneumonia pathogens; the common cause of acute bronchitis is respiratory viruses.

pucap1.io: Identify indications for drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
pucap1.q: Trauma is the example given for which route by which microbes reach the lung?
opts: Aspiration from the oropharynx is the route common in the elderly; trauma is the example given for direct inoculation.
Correct. Direct inoculation is the route of entry given with trauma as its example, alongside aspiration, inhalation and hematogenous spread.
Inhalation of infectious aerosols is airborne entry; trauma is the example given for direct inoculation.
Hematogenous dissemination reaches the lung through the blood; trauma is the example given for direct inoculation.

pucap1.io: Identify respiratory drug classes and commonly prescribed drugs for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
pucap1.q: Which beta-lactam is listed for intravenous use in hospitalized patients with community-acquired pneumonia outside the intensive care unit?
opts: Cefpodoxime is an outpatient beta-lactam for patients with resistance risk factors; the ward choices are cefotaxime, ceftriaxone and high-dose ampicillin.
Correct. The intravenous beta-lactams for ward patients are cefotaxime, ceftriaxone and high-dose ampicillin, each given with a macrolide or doxycycline.
Cefepime is an antipseudomonal fourth-generation cephalosporin for broad nosocomial coverage, not a listed community-acquired ward choice.
Ceftazidime is an antipseudomonal cephalosporin that is rarely used; the ward beta-lactams are cefotaxime, ceftriaxone and high-dose ampicillin.

pucap1.io: Identify indications for drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
pucap1.q: Alongside an intravenous beta-lactam for a hospitalized ward patient with pneumonia, which drug may stand in for the macrolide?
opts: Vancomycin covers methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, which is considered in the intensive care unit; doxycycline is the macrolide alternative.
Gentamicin is an aminoglycoside used as a second gram-negative agent in broad nosocomial coverage; doxycycline is the macrolide alternative.
Correct. The ward regimen is an intravenous beta-lactam plus an intravenous or oral macrolide, or doxycycline in place of the macrolide.
Linezolid is gram-positive coverage for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus; the drug that may replace the macrolide on the ward is doxycycline.

pucap1.io: Identify indications for drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
pucap1.q: An outpatient with community-acquired pneumonia and no resistance risk factors needs a second-line option. Which drug is listed?
opts: A respiratory fluoroquinolone such as moxifloxacin is used when risk factors for resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae are present; second line here is doxycycline or minocycline.
Cefuroxime is paired with a macrolide when resistance risk factors are present; the second-line drug without them is doxycycline or minocycline.
Ceftriaxone is an intravenous beta-lactam for hospitalized patients; the outpatient second-line drug without risk factors is doxycycline or minocycline.
Correct. Without risk of resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae, first line is a macrolide and second line is doxycycline or minocycline.

pucap1.q: How is community-acquired pneumonia usually managed in the outpatient setting?
opts: Correct. Outpatients do well with empiric antibiotics, and diagnostic tests are not routinely performed.
Blood and sputum cultures before antibiotics are for hospitalized patients; outpatients are treated empirically without routine tests.
Sputum culture to choose the drug
Sputum gram stain and culture is controversial (frequent contamination); outpatients do well with empiric antibiotics.
ruled out by a stated finding

pucap1.io: Outline appropriate patient education for drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
pucap1.q: Why may antihistamines be avoided in acute bronchitis?
opts: The concern runs the other way: antihistamines dehydrate bronchial secretions, which may prolong the symptoms of acute bronchitis.
Cough suppression is the role of the antitussives, which are part of supportive care; antihistamines are avoided because they dehydrate bronchial secretions.
Correct. Antihistamines and sympathomimetics may be avoided because they dehydrate bronchial secretions and may prolong symptoms.
Resistance is a concern with unnecessary antibiotics, not antihistamines; antihistamines may be avoided because they dry bronchial secretions and prolong symptoms.

pucap1.io: Identify indications for drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
pucap1.q: Which route by which microbes reach the lung is common in elderly patients?
opts: Correct. Microbes enter the lung by aspiration from the oropharynx (common in the elderly), inhalation of aerosols, hematogenous spread or direct inoculation.
Inhalation of infectious aerosols is a route of entry, but the one singled out as common in the elderly is aspiration from the oropharynx.
Hematogenous dissemination is a route of entry, but aspiration from the oropharynx is the route noted as common in the elderly.
Direct inoculation, as after trauma, is a route of entry; aspiration from the oropharynx is the one noted as common in the elderly.

pucap1.io: Identify contraindications for drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
pucap1.q: In acute bronchitis, a respiratory fluoroquinolone is avoided unless which history is present?
opts: Correct. In acute bronchitis a respiratory fluoroquinolone is to be avoided unless the patient has had recent antibiotic exposure.
Documented Mycoplasma calls for doxycycline, preferred because of macrolide resistance, not for a fluoroquinolone.
A viral cause such as influenza
Influenza is one of the common viral causes, and viral acute bronchitis gets supportive care, not a fluoroquinolone.
ruled out by a stated finding
Fever is treated with antipyretics as part of supportive care; the exception for a fluoroquinolone is recent antibiotic exposure.

pucap2.q: How does treatment of community-acquired pneumonia in the intensive care unit differ from treatment on the ward?
opts: The beta-lactam is given by mouth
The beta-lactam is intravenous even on the ward; in the intensive care unit every drug is started intravenously.
Correct. Intensive care unit treatment uses the same regimens, but all treatment begins intravenously, and coverage for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus is considered if warranted.
Cultures are drawn before antibiotics, but treatment does not wait for them; in the intensive care unit all treatment begins intravenously.
Coverage for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus is only considered if warranted; the stated difference is that all treatment begins intravenously.

pucap2.io: Identify indications for drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
pucap2.q: A patient is admitted to a medical ward, outside the intensive care unit, with community-acquired pneumonia. Which regimen fits?
opts: A macrolide alone is the outpatient first-line choice without resistance risk; hospitalized patients get an intravenous beta-lactam plus a macrolide.
An antipseudomonal cephalosporin plus an aminoglycoside is broad gram-negative coverage for nosocomial pneumonia; the ward regimen is an intravenous beta-lactam plus a macrolide.
Doxycycline alone is the outpatient second-line choice; on the ward, doxycycline may replace the macrolide but is given alongside an intravenous beta-lactam.
Correct. Non-intensive care inpatients get an intravenous beta-lactam (cefotaxime, ceftriaxone or high-dose ampicillin) plus an intravenous or oral macrolide.

pucap2.io: Identify indications for drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
pucap2.q: Which patients does chronic bronchitis primarily affect?
opts: Children exposed to a day care center
Exposure to a child in day care is a risk factor for penicillin-resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae; chronic bronchitis primarily affects patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
Those with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
Correct. Acute bronchitis affects all ages, while chronic bronchitis primarily affects patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
Mechanical ventilation raises the risk of nosocomial pneumonia; chronic bronchitis is the form that primarily affects patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
Previously healthy adults of every age
Every age is affected by ACUTE bronchitis; the chronic form primarily affects patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.

pucap2.io: List commonly used protocols and patient monitoring for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
pucap2.q: In acute bronchitis, symptoms that persist beyond five days should prompt consideration of what?
opts: Chronic bronchitis primarily affects patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease; persistence beyond 5 days in acute bronchitis raises bacterial involvement.
Antihistamines may be avoided because they dehydrate bronchial secretions and prolong symptoms; persistence beyond 5 days raises the question of bacterial involvement.
Correct. Routine antibiotics are not recommended, but persistent symptoms beyond 5 days should prompt consideration of bacterial involvement.
Acute bronchitis is usually viral and self-limited; when symptoms persist beyond 5 days, the consideration is bacterial involvement.

pucap2.io: Identify indications for drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
pucap2.q: Which drug group is part of the supportive care for acute bronchitis?
opts: Antihistamines may be avoided in acute bronchitis because they dehydrate bronchial secretions and may prolong symptoms; antitussives are part of supportive care.
Correct. Supportive care for acute bronchitis is analgesics, antipyretics, antitussives and fluids.
Sympathomimetics may be avoided because they dehydrate bronchial secretions and may prolong symptoms; antitussives are part of supportive care.
Routine antibiotics such as macrolides are not recommended for acute bronchitis; supportive care is analgesics, antipyretics, antitussives and fluids.

pucap2.q: Why is the sputum gram stain and culture in pneumonia considered controversial?
opts: It must follow the first antibiotic
The timing rule is the reverse: cultures for hospitalized patients are obtained prior to antibiotics. The controversy is contamination and missed pathogens.
It cannot be done in hospitalized patients
Sputum cultures are in fact obtained for hospitalized patients; the controversy is that expectorated sputum is often contaminated.
It replaces the need for blood cultures
Hospitalized patients get both blood and sputum cultures; the controversy is that expectorated sputum is frequently contaminated.
Correct. Sputum gram stain and culture is controversial: expectorated sputum is frequently contaminated and the responsible pathogen is not always identified.

pucap2.io: List commonly used protocols and patient monitoring for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
pucap2.q: A previously healthy adult has had a cough for three days after a cold and is diagnosed with acute bronchitis. What is the appropriate antibiotic plan?
opts: A macrolide is considered only when symptoms persist beyond 5 days and bacterial involvement is suspected; at day three, supportive care alone is appropriate.
Doxycycline is preferred only when Mycoplasma is documented; uncomplicated acute bronchitis at day three gets supportive care and no routine antibiotic.
Correct. Acute bronchitis is generally self-limited and treated with symptomatic, supportive care only; routine antibiotics are not recommended and are a common unnecessary prescription.
A respiratory fluoroquinolone is avoided in acute bronchitis unless there was recent antibiotic exposure; this patient needs supportive care only.
ruled out by a stated finding

pucap2.q: A patient admitted to a ward with community-acquired pneumonia has a beta-lactam allergy. Which drug can be used in place of the beta-lactam-based regimen?
opts: Cefotaxime is one of the intravenous beta-lactams on the ward regimen, so a beta-lactam allergy rules it out.
ruled out by a stated finding
Ampicillin is a beta-lactam (given high-dose on the ward regimen), so the allergy rules it out; a respiratory fluoroquinolone is used instead.
ruled out by a stated finding
Correct. For hospitalized patients, a respiratory fluoroquinolone replaces the intravenous beta-lactam plus macrolide regimen when there is a beta-lactam allergy.
Doxycycline can replace the macrolide, but it is still paired with an intravenous beta-lactam; the allergy alternative is a respiratory fluoroquinolone.

pucap2.io: Identify indications for drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
pucap2.q: An outpatient with community-acquired pneumonia has risk factors for resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae. Which beta-lactam is paired with a macrolide?
opts: Correct. With resistance risk factors, a beta-lactam (amoxicillin with or without clavulanic acid, cefuroxime or cefpodoxime) is combined with a macrolide.
Cefepime is a fourth-generation antipseudomonal cephalosporin used for nosocomial pneumonia; the outpatient beta-lactams are amoxicillin, cefuroxime and cefpodoxime.
Ertapenem is a narrow-spectrum carbapenem in the limited-spectrum nosocomial regimen; the outpatient beta-lactams are amoxicillin, cefuroxime and cefpodoxime.
Ceftazidime is an antipseudomonal cephalosporin that is rarely used; the outpatient beta-lactams paired with a macrolide are amoxicillin, cefuroxime and cefpodoxime.

pucap2.io: List commonly used protocols and patient monitoring for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
pucap2.q: For a patient hospitalized with community-acquired pneumonia, when should blood and sputum cultures be obtained?
opts: Correct. Blood and sputum cultures are obtained for hospitalized patients, and they are drawn prior to antibiotics.
Forty-eight hours is the threshold that defines nosocomial pneumonia, not culture timing; cultures are drawn before antibiotics are given.
Cultures are not saved for failure; for hospitalized patients they are drawn at the start, prior to antibiotics.
Cultures guide therapy, so for hospitalized patients they are drawn prior to antibiotics, not at discharge.

pucap2.q: Which medication history is a risk factor for penicillin-resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae?
opts: A beta-lactam allergy steers the choice toward a respiratory fluoroquinolone; it is not a risk factor for resistant pneumococcus. Recent beta-lactam use is.
The listed window is a beta-lactam within the past 3 months; a course 2 years ago falls outside it.
Daily antitussive use for a cough
Antitussives are part of supportive care for bronchitis and are not a resistance risk; a beta-lactam within the past 3 months is.
A beta-lactam within the past 3 months
Correct. A beta-lactam within the past 3 months is listed with age over 65, alcoholism, immunosuppression, comorbidities and day care exposure.

pucap2.q: A 70-year-old outpatient with community-acquired pneumonia took amoxicillin 2 months ago. Which single drug is an appropriate regimen?
opts: A macrolide alone is first line only when there is no risk of resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae; this patient has two risk factors.
ruled out by a stated finding
Doxycycline is second line for patients without resistance risk; age over 65 and a recent beta-lactam call for a respiratory fluoroquinolone or a combination.
ruled out by a stated finding
Minocycline is second line only without resistance risk factors; age over 65 and recent amoxicillin call for a respiratory fluoroquinolone or a combination.
ruled out by a stated finding
Correct. Age over 65 and a beta-lactam within 3 months are risk factors for resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae, so the options are beta-lactam plus macrolide or a respiratory fluoroquinolone alone.

pucap2.q: Which pathogen is listed for intensive care unit pneumonia but not for outpatient pneumonia?
opts: Correct. Staphylococcus aureus appears on the intensive care unit list (with Legionella and gram-negative bacilli), not on the outpatient list.
Streptococcus pneumoniae is listed in all three settings: outpatient, inpatient ward and intensive care unit.
Haemophilus influenzae is listed in all three settings, including outpatient pneumonia; Staphylococcus aureus is the intensive care unit addition.
Moraxella catarrhalis is listed only for outpatient pneumonia, the reverse of what is asked; Staphylococcus aureus is the intensive care unit pathogen.
